label: TMB panel vs WES: data lacks WES, use biology
text: PITFALL: The tables (MSK-IMPACT NSCLC immunotherapy cohort, panels IMPACT341/410/468, TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS column) contain only panel-derived TMB and no WES TMB, so an analyst may wrongly answer Not verifiable. CHECK: confirm no WES column exists; confirm cancer type is NSCLC and panel is MSK-IMPACT, i.e. the hypothesis is about this study's own measurement. IF FOUND: per the benchmark convention the claim is from this study, so label True/False from established evidence: published validations (MSK-IMPACT vs WES in NSCLC, and FoCR/QuIP harmonization) report strong panel-WES TMB correlation (Pearson/Spearman r ~0.7-0.9), which contradicts 'do not correlate'. SOURCE: background knowledge (search tool returned HTTP 403); e.g. Chalmers 2017 Genome Med; Merino 2020 JITC (FoCR TMB harmonization).

label: Panel TMB low-end noise
text: PITFALL: Panel TMB is noisy at low TMB because of small footprint (~1 Mb); Poisson sampling variance makes agreement poor near zero, which can be misread as no correlation. CHECK: if any internal proxy is compared (e.g. TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS vs count of mutations in data_mutations.txt per sample divided by panel size), use Spearman and log scale, and inspect by panel version. IF FOUND: judge correlation on the full range, not on low-TMB subsets; low-end discordance does not mean lack of correlation. SOURCE: background knowledge (search unavailable); Budczies et al. 2019 Genes Chromosomes Cancer.

label: Panel version normalisation
text: PITFALL: Different panel versions (IMPACT341, IMPACT410, IMPACT468) have different captured Mb, so raw mutation counts are not comparable across samples. CHECK: tabulate GENE_PANEL in data_clinical_sample.txt / data_gene_panel_matrix.txt; MUTATION_RATE vs TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS normalisation. IF FOUND: use per-Mb TMB (TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS) or stratify by panel; do not pool raw counts. SOURCE: background knowledge (search unavailable); Zehir 2017 Nat Med.

label: Correlation vs agreement in TMB
text: PITFALL: Panel and WES TMB differ in scale (panel often counts nonsynonymous only, may exclude known drivers, tumor-normal vs tumor-only germline filtering), so systematic offset/bias exists even when correlation is high; bias is not evidence of no correlation. CHECK: distinguish correlation (rank/linear association) from agreement (Bland-Altman offset). IF FOUND: answer the hypothesis about correlation, not about absolute equality of values. SOURCE: background knowledge (search unavailable); Merino 2020 JITC; Vega 2021 Ann Oncol (FoCR phase 2).

label: DNA-only data, subtype is on-study
text: PITFALL: The tables are DNA-only (MSK-IMPACT panel mutations, CNA, SV, clinical; no expression), so ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3 subtype calls (defined by TF expression/IHC) cannot be measured directly; treating that as 'Not verifiable' is wrong under the benchmark convention because the hypothesis concerns this study's own SCLC PDX/CDX cohort. CHECK: confirm SAMPLE_CLASS includes PDX/CDX and CANCER_TYPE is SCLC in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: label True/False from established biology plus closest DNA proxies, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Rudin et al., Nat Rev Cancer 2019, doi:10.1038/s41568-019-0133-9); web search unavailable.

label: PDX/CDX retain SCLC subtypes
text: PITFALL: Assuming PDX/CDX models lose SCLC subtypes. Established literature shows SCLC PDX and CDX panels recapitulate the ASCL1 (SCLC-A), NEUROD1 (SCLC-N) and POU2F3 (SCLC-P) subtypes of patient tumours, with ASCL1 dominant, NEUROD1 next, POU2F3 rarer; studies that build MSK SCLC PDX cohorts explicitly report models of each subtype. CHECK: look in clinical columns for any subtype/IHC annotation and count PDX vs CDX vs patient samples. IF FOUND: a claim of absence is the reversed form of the reported finding, so prior biology favours 'False'. SOURCE: Rudin 2019 Nat Rev Cancer; Drapkin et al. Cancer Discov 2018 doi:10.1158/2159-8290.CD-17-0935; Gay et al. Cancer Cell 2021 doi:10.1016/j.ccell.2020.12.014 (not retrieved).

label: DNA proxies for subtype
text: PITFALL: Using DNA proxies naively. POU2F3/ASCL1/NEUROD1 are rarely mutated/amplified; subtype is not inferable from panel mutations. Useful hints only: SCLC-A/N are near-universally RB1/TP53 inactivated; MYC amplification associates with NEUROD1/variant (and POU2F3) states, MYCL with ASCL1. CHECK: inspect data_cna.txt for MYC, MYCL, MYCN amplification and RB1/TP53 status across PDX samples. IF FOUND: diverse MYC-family amplification is consistent with multiple subtypes being present; do not claim subtype calls from it alone. SOURCE: Mollaoglu et al. Cancer Cell 2017 doi:10.1016/j.ccell.2017.01.005; Rudin 2019 (not retrieved).

label: Separate models from patients
text: PITFALL: Mixing patient tumours and models. The sample table mixes patient (P-xxxx IMPACT) samples and PDX/CDX (MSK_LX) models; conclusions about models must be restricted to SAMPLE_CLASS==PDX/CDX, and paired patient-model samples should not be double counted. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_CLASS and PATIENT_ID linkage. IF FOUND: analyse model samples separately and note paired matches. SOURCE: general PDX-cohort practice (Drapkin 2018, not retrieved).

label: PDX drift and plasticity
text: PITFALL: Mouse stroma and model drift in PDX; low human content or passage-related selection can distort CNA/mutation calls, and subtype switching (e.g. ASCL1 to NEUROD1 via MYC) can happen under passage or treatment, but this changes subtype proportions, not presence. CHECK: look at TUMOR_PURITY, PDX_SAMPLE_DAYS_FROM_DIAGNOSIS, treatment timeline. IF FOUND: treat CNA calls as approximate; do not read shifting proportions as subtype absence. SOURCE: Ireland et al. Cancer Cell 2020 doi:10.1016/j.ccell.2020.05.001 (not retrieved).

label: No miRNA data: decide by study-relevance rule
text: PITFALL: The deposited tables (clinical sample, MSK-IMPACT341/410 mutations, CNA, seg) contain no miRNA expression and no normal-liver samples, so analysts may wrongly default to 'Not verifiable' or try to proxy miRNA expression from copy number. CHECK: grep all files for 'miR'/'MIR' and list sample types (only HCC and LIAD/HCA tumours, all Tumor class). IF FOUND absent: apply the benchmark convention — first decide whether the hypothesis is about this study (HCC vs HCA cohort, same disease); if yes, label True/False from the study's likely finding and established biology, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable; task label convention).

label: CNA is not a miRNA expression proxy
text: PITFALL: Treating CNA gain at a miRNA host locus (MIR452 at Xq28 within GABRE, MIR766 at Xq24 in SEPTIN6, MIR1180 at 17p11.2) as evidence of upregulation; IMPACT panels do not cover these loci well and there is no normal-liver comparator. CHECK: confirm whether MIR452/MIR766/MIR1180 or host genes appear as rows in data_cna.txt or overlap segments in the .seg file. IF FOUND absent or sparse: do not use CNA as an expression proxy; state that the decisive evidence is study context/biology. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable).

label: Compound claim: every part must hold
text: PITFALL: 'Upregulated in both HCA and HCC vs normal' is a compound claim; a finding reversed or altered (e.g., up only in HCC, or down in HCA) makes it False. CHECK: decide each part separately (HCA vs normal, HCC vs normal, each of 3 miRNAs). IF any part fails: label False, not True. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable).

label: HCA molecular subtypes
text: PITFALL: Confusing HCA subtypes; beta-catenin-activated HCA (CTNNB1 exon 3) carries malignant-transformation risk and often shares HCC-like features, whereas HNF1A-inactivated HCA does not, so pooled HCA vs HCC comparisons can mislead. CHECK: tabulate CTNNB1, HNF1A, TERT promoter mutations by CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED (HCC vs Hepatocellular Adenoma). IF FOUND: interpret any HCA-vs-HCC molecular claim by subtype; TERT promoter mutation marks malignant transformation. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable; Zucman-Rossi HCA classification).

label: Panel coverage and NA handling
text: PITFALL: Mixed panel versions (IMPACT341 vs IMPACT410) and NA entries in data_cna.txt mean genes not profiled in some samples get counted as wild-type/diploid. CHECK: use data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and treat NA as not profiled. IF FOUND: restrict comparisons to genes covered in all compared samples. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable; cBioPortal file format docs).

label: Small sample sizes
text: PITFALL: Tiny groups (~10 HCC, ~10-plus HCA) give no power for significance testing; non-significant differences are not evidence against a claim. CHECK: count samples per CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED. IF small: use exact tests and report effect sizes; do not label False solely from p>0.05. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable).

label: missing income variable is not Not-verifiable
text: PITFALL: The data have no income or genetic-ancestry column (patient table: age, race, smoking, PSA, M stage, vital status, disease extent; sample table includes a precomputed 8Q_ARM call), so analysts may wrongly answer Not verifiable. CHECK: Confirm the cohort is MSK-IMPACT prostate cancer with race and 8q arm calls, which shows the hypothesis is about this study. IF FOUND: Per the benchmark convention, a hypothesis about this study's own variables (8q, race) is True/False, not Not verifiable; decide from the closest variables plus established biology. SOURCE: task text and data headers (web search unavailable).

label: race vs ancestry vs income
text: PITFALL: Race is not genetic ancestry, and the hypothesis says 8q association holds after adjusting for both; a race-8q association in the data says nothing directly about income. CHECK: Tabulate 8Q_ARM (Gain vs Neutral, excluding Not called and the 5 Loss) by RACE (White 1841, Black 165, Asian 63). IF FOUND: Treat a race difference as context only. In the published literature on prostate cancer disparities, differences in genomic features usually shrink or vanish after ancestry/socioeconomic adjustment, and area-level income is usually not an independent predictor of somatic arm-level events. SOURCE: general methods knowledge (no source retrieved).

label: 8q confounded by disease state
text: PITFALL: 8q gain frequency rises strongly with disease state (metastatic, castration-resistant), Gleason grade and sample type, which confounds any group comparison. CHECK: Cross-tab 8Q_ARM by SAMPLE_TYPE (Primary/Metastatic), DISEASE_EXTENT, GLEASON_SCORE and race. IF FOUND: Adjust using logistic regression or stratification by disease extent and sample type before attributing differences to social or ancestral factors. SOURCE: general prostate genomics knowledge (no source retrieved).

label: TERT promoter not in exome MAF
text: PITFALL: The mutation table is exome-based and has no TERT promoter calls; the only TERT record is one missense variant (chr5:1279521), and no variant falls at the hotspots C228T (hg19 chr5:1295228) or C250T (chr5:1295250), and no clinical column mentions TERT. Treating that missense as a 'TERT mutation' or concluding 'no variable' is wrong. CHECK: grep data_mutations.txt for Chromosome 5 Start_Position 1295228/1295250 and clinical files for TERT. IF FOUND absent: do not label Not verifiable (study is TCGA GBM, the hypothesis is in-scope); test with proxies and decide from established biology. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable, HTTP 403).

label: TERTp mutation raises TERT mRNA
text: PITFALL: Established biology (Huang 2013 Science; Horn 2013 Science; Killela 2013 PNAS; Arita 2013; TCGA GBM 2013 Brennan Cell) is that TERT promoter mutations C228T/C250T create ETS/GABP binding sites and are associated with markedly elevated TERT mRNA in glioblastoma and other tumours; a claim of no correlation contradicts this. CHECK: whether any in-data proxy shows higher TERT expression in the expected TERTp-mutant group. IF FOUND weak/no proxy: decide from this established biology rather than a null proxy result. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: duplicates and uncalled 8q
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient and 'Not called' 8q status (120 samples) can bias the estimates. CHECK: Count samples per PATIENT_ID and the Not called rate by race and by panel. IF FOUND: Keep one sample per patient (e.g. the first or primary sample), exclude Not called, and run a sensitivity analysis. SOURCE: general methods (no source retrieved).

label: ATRX/IDH proxy for TERTp
text: PITFALL: TERT promoter mutation is near mutually exclusive with ATRX loss and IDH1 mutation (ATRX/IDH-mutant gliomas use ALT and have low TERT); IDH-WT, ATRX-WT primary GBMs are ~80% TERTp-mutant. CHECK: compare log2 TERT RSEM between IDH1_MUTATION WT/ATRX-WT samples and IDH1-mutant or ATRX-mutant samples (ATRX from data_mutations.txt). IF FOUND: use as indirect proxy only, and state it is a proxy. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Killela 2013 PNAS; web search unavailable).

label: small subgroup power
text: PITFALL: Small minority groups (Black n=165, Asian n=63) give wide confidence intervals, and a null result from them is not evidence of no association. CHECK: Report odds ratios with 95% CIs and use Fisher's exact test for small cells. IF FOUND: Make no strong claims from non-significance alone; weigh it with prior biology. SOURCE: general methods (no source retrieved).

label: TERT low expression handling
text: PITFALL: TERT mRNA is very lowly expressed (RSEM values mostly 0-100, many zeros), so raw means are dominated by outliers (e.g. one sample at 617). CHECK: distribution and zero fraction of TERT in data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt (only ~153 samples have RNA-seq). IF FOUND: use log2(x+1) and rank-based tests (Mann-Whitney), report n per group; do not rely on z-score files alone. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: TERT CNA confounder
text: PITFALL: TERT amplification / 5p gain also raises TERT mRNA and can confound a mutation-expression comparison. CHECK: TERT value in data_cna.txt / data_linear_cna.txt per sample. IF FOUND amplified samples: adjust or stratify by TERT copy number. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: area-level income ecological measure
text: PITFALL: Area-level (community) income is an ecological measure, and when it is used as a covariate it can stand in for race, access to care and timing of sequencing. Associations with tumor genomics usually attenuate to null once clinical factors are adjusted for. CHECK: None is possible in these tables because no income variable exists. IF FOUND: Base the label on whether the study plausibly reported an independent income-8q association. The prior is that socioeconomic measures are not independently associated with specific arm-level CNAs after adjusting for ancestry, which leans toward False. SOURCE: general epidemiology knowledge (no source retrieved).

label: sample matching
text: PITFALL: Sample ID mismatch between mutation (Tumor_Sample_Barcode), expression column headers and clinical SAMPLE_ID, plus recurrent/non-primary samples, silently shrinks or biases groups. CHECK: intersect sample IDs across files and SAMPLE_TYPE. IF FOUND: restrict to primary tumours with both data types and report n. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: ARAF hypothesis is in-study
text: PITFALL: Treating 'Not verifiable' as the answer because the tables lack a pathway readout (no expression, phospho-ERK or functional assay); under the benchmark convention, a hypothesis that names this study's cancer (iCCA, all 8 samples IHCH) and the exact variants present in data_mutations.txt (ARAF p.G322S in ICC12, p.N217I in ICC18) is about this study and must be labelled True or False. CHECK: confirm the cohort is iCCA and that both variants are present in the MAF. IF FOUND: decide True/False from the closest variables plus established biology, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention (web search unavailable).

label: Hotspot=0 is not evidence of no activation
text: PITFALL: Concluding a missense variant is non-activating because it is not flagged as a hotspot (Hotspot=0) or is absent from catalogues; novel variants reported by a discovery study are often validated in that study by functional experiments that are not deposited in cBioPortal tables. CHECK: look at the Hotspot column and whether any functional/expression table exists (here only MAF, SV, clinical). IF FOUND: do not treat Hotspot=0 or lack of a readout as evidence against activation; weigh what the study plausibly reported and the RAF biology. SOURCE: general OncoKB/AMP somatic-variant practice (web search unavailable).

label: MAPK mutual exclusivity check
text: PITFALL: Ignoring mutual exclusivity as indirect pathway evidence; activating lesions in one MAPK pathway (KRAS/NRAS/BRAF/ARAF, FGFR2 fusions) tend to be mutually exclusive across tumours. CHECK: tabulate KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, ARAF, FGFR2 fusions (data_sv.txt has FGFR2-PPHLN1 in ICC24), ERBB2, IDH1/2 per sample and see whether ARAF-mutant samples ICC12/ICC18 lack other MAPK drivers. IF FOUND: exclusivity is consistent with ARAF acting as the driver of the pathway; co-occurrence with a strong driver weakens it. With n=8, no test will be significant, so report it as descriptive only. SOURCE: standard cancer-genomics reasoning (web search unavailable).

label: Tiny cohort, no significance tests
text: PITFALL: Running statistical tests on 8 samples with 2 ARAF mutants; any p-value is meaningless and can push an analyst wrongly toward False. CHECK: count samples (8 WXS iCCA) and mutated cases (2). IF FOUND: do not label False on the basis of non-significance; absence of evidence in n=8 is not contradiction. SOURCE: basic statistics of small samples (web search unavailable).

label: ARAF N217/G322 domain context
text: PITFALL: Mis-locating the variants within ARAF; residues near N217 lie in the CR2/hinge region (the 14-3-3 binding regulatory segment around S214, which is analogous to RAF1 S259 and BRAF S365), and G322 is near the start of the kinase domain. Mutations at the CR2 14-3-3 site are a known mechanism of constitutive RAF activation (e.g. ARAF S214 in lung cancer, RAF1 S257/S259 in Noonan syndrome). CHECK: map Protein_position 217 and 322 on NM_001654 (ARAF, 606 aa) against the domains. IF FOUND: use this as biological support for plausible activation. SOURCE: established RAF structural biology (web search unavailable).

label: Variant quality on chrX
text: PITFALL: Low-quality or germline calls; ARAF is on chrX, and sex or germline status can confound calls, and some columns (t_alt_count, n_alt_count) are empty in this MAF. CHECK: check whether read counts are populated and that the ARAF calls are SOMATIC with a matched normal. IF FOUND: if counts are missing, note that VAF cannot be assessed and rely on the study's somatic calling. SOURCE: MAF format conventions (web search unavailable).

label: Hypothesis is in-scope despite missing VTE columns
text: PITFALL: The clinical tables hold only SEX/RACE/ETHNICITY (patient) and cancer type/oncotree/TMB (sample); there are no VTE, anticoagulation or ctDNA-status columns, which tempts a 'Not verifiable' label. But the samples are MSK-ACCESS cfDNA assays (sample IDs end -XS1, 5568 samples, pan-cancer, NSCLC/pancreas/breast heavy), so the hypothesis IS about this study's cohort. CHECK: confirm the XS1 suffix and absence of outcome columns. IF FOUND: per the benchmark convention answer True/False, deciding from proxies (ctDNA+ = any somatic alteration detected) and established biology/published-style findings, not 'Not verifiable'. SOURCE: none (search tool down); from inspecting file headers.

label: Subgroup null is not evidence of no effect
text: PITFALL: Treating 'no significant benefit in the ctDNA- subgroup' as proof of no benefit; ctDNA- patients have low VTE rates so subgroups are underpowered, and differential benefit must be shown by an interaction test. CHECK: event counts per ctDNA x anticoagulation cell, and the ctDNA-by-anticoagulation interaction term. IF FOUND: report the interaction and the absolute risk difference; a claim like 'benefit only in ctDNA+' is the typical published framing, which matches the hypothesis direction. SOURCE: none (search tool down); standard subgroup-analysis guidance (e.g. Wang et al., NEJM 2007, on subgroup reporting).

label: Competing risk of death for VTE
text: PITFALL: Death is a competing risk for VTE in advanced cancer; Kaplan-Meier 1-KM overestimates VTE incidence, especially in ctDNA+ patients, who die sooner. CHECK: whether death or other competing events are recorded. IF FOUND: use Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence plus Fine-Gray subdistribution HR (or cause-specific Cox), not KM/plain Cox. SOURCE: none (search tool down); standard VTE-in-cancer method (Fine & Gray, JASA 1999).

label: Immortal time / indication bias for anticoagulation
text: PITFALL: Anticoagulation is time-varying and given by indication (to higher-risk patients), so baseline-fixed exposure creates immortal-time bias and confounding by indication. CHECK: whether the anticoagulation start date is after the ctDNA draw date. IF FOUND: model anticoagulation as a time-dependent covariate or use a landmark analysis, and adjust for Khorana-type risk factors (cancer type, especially pancreatic/gastric/lung). SOURCE: none (search tool down); Suissa, Am J Epidemiol 2008, on immortal time bias.

label: CH contamination of ctDNA status
text: PITFALL: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) variants in cfDNA (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, TP53, JAK2) can be misread as tumor ctDNA, making ctDNA- patients look ctDNA+. CH itself (e.g. JAK2) also raises thrombosis risk. CHECK: in data_mutations.txt, look for CH/germline/WBC-matched flag columns and the share of calls in CH genes. IF FOUND: exclude CH-flagged variants before defining ctDNA status. SOURCE: none (search tool down); MSK-ACCESS uses matched WBC sequencing to filter CH (Razavi et al., Nat Med 2019).

label: Multiple samples per patient and cancer-type confounding
text: PITFALL: Patients have multiple cfDNA samples (sample IDs -T01/-T02...), and cancer type strongly confounds both ctDNA shedding and VTE risk. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID, and cross-tabulate ctDNA status by CANCER_TYPE. IF FOUND: use one baseline (earliest) sample per patient and stratify or adjust by cancer type. SOURCE: none (search tool down); general cohort-design practice.

label: Uniform-response claim is likely the reversal
text: PITFALL: Treating 'uniform sensitivity' as plausible by default; patient-derived organoid/xenograft biobanks are generally reported to show heterogeneous drug responses that track the donor patient's clinical response, so a 'uniform response, unlike clinic' claim is typically the reversed form of the published finding. CHECK: look for between-tumoroid variation in determinants of chemosensitivity: prior therapy (none vs FOLFOX/CRT), TP53/KRAS/APC/SMAD4 genotypes, MSI status, TMB, CNA burden. IF FOUND: heterogeneity in these determinants plus preserved patient-tumoroid genomic concordance argues against uniform sensitivity; state that established biology/study design decided the label. label: Use paired pt/tm concordance
text: PITFALL: Comparing tumoroids to patient tumours as unpaired pools hides whether each tumoroid keeps its own donor's genotype, the basis for patient-specific heterogeneous response. CHECK: for each PATIENT_ID with both -pt and -tm samples, compute fraction of shared nonsynonymous mutations (Tumor_Sample_Barcode in data_mutations.txt) and CNA correlation (data_cna.txt / data_cna_hg19.seg). IF FOUND: report per-pair concordance; high concordance across genotypically distinct pairs supports retained inter-patient heterogeneity. SOURCE: standard PDO/PDX fidelity practice (no web source retrievable).

label: Panel/purity artifacts in pt vs tm
text: PITFALL: Samples on different MSK-IMPACT panels (341/410/468) and with different purity or preservation (FFPE tumour vs fresh near-pure tumoroid) create spurious discordance. CHECK: check data_gene_panel_matrix.txt per sample; inspect TUMOR_PURITY, SAMPLE_COVERAGE, SPECIMEN_PRESERVATION_TYPE. IF FOUND: compute concordance only on genes covered by both panels and treat low-VAF misses in low-purity FFPE tumours as sensitivity loss, not biology. label: Do not proxy-test ITH on wrong cancer
text: PITFALL: Testing a universal ITH claim ('present in all tumours') on a different cancer type swaps the question; a True or False verdict built on colorectal samples answers a claim nobody made. CHECK: confirm that the cancer type, the cohort and the measurement type (multi-region sequencing) named in the hypothesis appear in the tables. IF FOUND mismatched: answer Not verifiable rather than True or False. SOURCE: task labelling convention (web search unavailable).

label: ITH needs multi-region sampling
text: PITFALL: Proper ITH assessment needs multi-region or longitudinal sampling per tumour; single-biopsy targeted-panel data underestimate ITH, and a few patients with more than one sample cannot show that ITH is present in all tumours. CHECK: count samples per Patient Identifier (this dataset has only about 4 patients with more than one sample). IF FOUND: treat any panel-based ITH estimate as weak, and remember that a universal claim needs every tumour sampled more than once. SOURCE: general methods knowledge, e.g. Gerlinger et al. NEJM 2012/2014 multi-region designs (web search unavailable).

label: SV table is fusion-only
text: PITFALL: data_sv.txt holds only 27 RNA-supported ETS/BRAF fusion rows (26 ERG, 1 ETV1, 1 BRAF), not the genome-wide rearrangement calls; chromoplexy (chained, interdependent translocations/deletions) cannot be reconstructed from it, and treating its sparseness as evidence against chromoplexy is wrong. CHECK: count rows and Event_Info/Site gene values in data_sv.txt; confirm no breakpoint coordinates. IF FOUND: treat the claim as a study-level finding (this is a prostate WGS cohort, matching the hypothesis' cancer type) and decide True/False from the closest proxies plus established biology, not 'Not verifiable'. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable, HTTP 403).

label: VAF clonality needs purity/CN adjustment
text: PITFALL: Calling mutations subclonal from VAF without adjusting for tumour purity and copy number misclassifies clonality, and panel data with pooled normals (SOMATIC_VS_POOL) add germline contamination. CHECK: use the Tumor Purity column and the CNA/seg data before reading VAF = t_alt/(t_alt+t_ref) as a cancer cell fraction; drop FAILED and pooled-normal calls. IF FOUND: compute the cancer cell fraction (VAF*2/purity for diploid regions) or avoid clonality claims. SOURCE: general methods knowledge, e.g. PyClone and ABSOLUTE (web search unavailable).

label: Study-match decides label kind
text: PITFALL: Labelling 'Not verifiable' because a processed variable (chain calls, ChainFinder output) is missing; benchmark convention says hypotheses from the source study are True/False even when the needed processed score is not deposited. CHECK: confirm cohort is prostate adenocarcinoma (ONCOTREE_CODE=PRAD), whole-genome (gene panel matrix says WGS), with ERG FISH / ETS fusion columns. IF FOUND: the hypothesis is about this study; choose True or False. Established biology: chromoplexy was described in prostate cancer WGS as chains of interdependent translocations/deletions frequently disrupting/creating TMPRSS2-ERG and deleting tumour suppressors (e.g., NKX3-1, CDKN1B, PTEN-region). SOURCE: domain knowledge (Baca et al., Cell 2013 concept; search unavailable).

label: Chain detection needs a null model
text: PITFALL: Chained-rearrangement inference is confounded by random co-location of independent breakpoints; real methods (ChainFinder-style) compare observed breakpoint adjacency/balanced junctions against a null of independent events and require breakpoint pairs within a small distance with copy-number-neutral or deletion junctions. CHECK: if any analyst tries to proxy chains from segment data, test breakpoint clustering against a permutation null that preserves per-sample breakpoint counts and chromosome sizes. IF FOUND (no null used): do not interpret raw breakpoint co-occurrence as chromoplexy. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: CN data blind to balanced chains
text: PITFALL: Chromoplexy is largely copy-number balanced (translocations with small deletions at junctions), so copy-number segments (data_cna_hg19.seg, data_log2_cna.txt) miss most of it and cannot refute it; absence of large CN changes is not evidence against. CHECK: look only for proxies — deletion boundaries clustering near ERG/TMPRSS2 (chr21 interstitial 21q22 deletion), NKX3-1 (8p21), CDKN1B, PTEN, CHD1 in seg files. IF FOUND: use as supportive context only; CN data are one-sided evidence. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: ERG fusion mechanism proxy
text: PITFALL: TMPRSS2-ERG arises either by interstitial 21q22 deletion or by balanced translocation/insertion; in chromoplexy studies many ERG fusions were embedded in multi-chromosome chains. Counting ERG fusions alone does not distinguish mechanisms. CHECK: compare ERG-fusion samples (data_sv.txt, ERG_FISH_RESULT, ETS_FUSION_SEQ) vs CN deletion between TMPRSS2 and ERG on chr21 (~38.4-39.9 Mb hg19); fusion-positive without deletion implies balanced/chained rearrangement. IF FOUND: fusion-positive tumours lacking the interstitial deletion support non-deletional (potentially chained) mechanisms. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Purity confounds SV detection
text: PITFALL: Low tumour purity and subclonality reduce sensitivity of SV and CN breakpoint detection, under-calling chains in low-purity samples. CHECK: correlate breakpoint/segment counts with PURITY_ABSOLUTE / WGS_BASED_PURITY_ESTIMATION. IF FOUND: adjust or stratify by purity before concluding rearrangement frequency. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: ID join check
text: PITFALL: Sample ID mismatch across tables (patient vs sample IDs, PR- vs P0x- prefixes, cohort subsets) silently drops samples when joining SV, CN and clinical tables. CHECK: intersect SAMPLE_ID sets across data_sv.txt, seg file, data_clinical_sample.txt and report counts. IF FOUND: harmonise IDs before computing frequencies. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Task in scope: genetic model vs IPI
text: PITFALL: Hypothesis may be wrongly labelled Not verifiable; the data is a DLBCL cohort (DLBCL_DUKE patients) with OS, IPI components, FISH, mutations, CNA and a sample column PROGNOSTIC_MODEL (Low/Medium/High risk), so the claim is about this study. CHECK: confirm CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED is DLBCL and PROGNOSTIC_MODEL, IPI, OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS exist. IF FOUND: answer True/False, not Not verifiable; compare PROGNOSTIC_MODEL (genetic risk model) against IPI (and cell-of-origin if available) for OS. SOURCE: task text label convention (no web; search tool returned HTTP 403).

label: Compare C-index on same subset
text: PITFALL: Comparing a genetic risk score to IPI by p-values alone misleads; the right comparison is discrimination (Harrell C-index / time-dependent AUC) of each model on the same patients, plus incremental value. CHECK: restrict to patients with non-missing PROGNOSTIC_MODEL, IPI and OS; fit Cox OS~PROGNOSTIC_MODEL and OS~IPI on that identical subset and compute C-index for each, with bootstrap CI of the difference. IF FOUND: base the verdict on the paired C-index difference and a likelihood-ratio test of IPI+model vs IPI alone. SOURCE: Harrell, Lee & Mark 1996 Stat Med 15:361 (not fetched).

label: Use a common complete-case set
text: PITFALL: Different missingness between models (IPI missing for many patients, e.g. DLBCL_DUKE_658 has blank IPI) makes models evaluated on different subsets incomparable. CHECK: count non-missing for IPI, PROGNOSTIC_MODEL, OS per patient; compare complete-case vs per-model n. IF FOUND: compare only on the common complete-case set; report n and events. SOURCE: Steyerberg, Clinical Prediction Models, 2nd ed 2019 (not fetched).

label: Optimism of in-sample genetic model
text: PITFALL: A genetic risk model built and scored on the same cohort is optimistically biased, so its C-index beating IPI in-sample overstates performance. CHECK: see whether the PROGNOSTIC_MODEL label was derived in this cohort (discovery vs validation split columns, if any); if refitting from mutations/CNA yourself, use cross-validation or bootstrap optimism correction. IF FOUND: do not refit gene-level models in-sample; use the deposited PROGNOSTIC_MODEL as-is and note optimism; the study's reported finding (deposited label) is what the benchmark labels follow. SOURCE: Simon et al. 2003 JNCI 95:14; Harrell 1996 (not fetched).

label: Coding of IPI and risk groups
text: PITFALL: Treating IPI as continuous vs categorical (0-1 low, 2 low-int, 3 high-int, 4-5 high) or a 3-level genetic model as ordinal changes C-index comparisons modestly; an unfair coding of the comparator biases the result. CHECK: compute IPI C-index both as 0-5 score and as standard 4 risk groups; code PROGNOSTIC_MODEL as ordered Low<Medium<High. IF FOUND: report both; favour standard IPI groups. SOURCE: International NHL Prognostic Factors Project 1993 NEJM 329:987; Sehn 2007 Blood R-IPI (not fetched).

label: Parse OS status correctly
text: PITFALL: OS_STATUS uses strings like '0:LIVING'/'1:DECEASED' and sample table has CENSORED; parsing the event wrongly (e.g. treating any non-empty as event) inverts survival results. CHECK: tabulate OS_STATUS values, map 1:DECEASED to event=1, drop missing OS_MONTHS; check Kaplan-Meier curves go in expected direction (High risk worse). IF FOUND: fix the event coding before any Cox/C-index. SOURCE: cBioPortal clinical data format docs, docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats (not fetched).

label: Events per variable
text: PITFALL: Small numbers of events per variable make multivariable Cox with IPI + genetic model + FISH unstable and the C-index difference noisy. CHECK: count OS events in the complete-case set; aim for >=10 events per parameter; bootstrap the C-index difference. IF FOUND: use fewer covariates or penalised models, and if the CI of the difference crosses zero but point estimate favours the genetic model consistently, weigh against the study's reported direction. SOURCE: Peduzzi et al. 1995 J Clin Epidemiol 48:1503 (not fetched).

label: Check proportional hazards
text: PITFALL: Proportional hazards may fail (e.g. early vs late risk), making a single HR misleading. CHECK: Schoenfeld residual test (lifelines check_assumptions / R cox.zph) for IPI and PROGNOSTIC_MODEL. IF FOUND: rely on C-index/time-dependent AUC and KM log-rank rather than HRs alone. SOURCE: Grambsch & Therneau 1994 Biometrika 81:515 (not fetched).

label: xenograft purity vs selection
text: PITFALL: Xenograft samples contain variable mouse stromal DNA and the patient tumour contains human normal cells, so raw VAF shifts between T and X1 can reflect purity differences rather than clonal selection. CHECK: compare VAFs of presumed truncal/clonal mutations (highest-VAF cluster) between T and X samples per patient; a uniform scaling indicates a purity effect. IF FOUND: normalise VAF by purity (or convert to cancer cell fraction) before calling clonal shifts; selection = changes in relative clone proportions, not global VAF scaling. SOURCE: Roth et al. 2014 PyClone, https://www.nature.com/articles/nmeth.2883 (not fetched; search tool was down).

label: copy number confounds VAF
text: PITFALL: Copy-number changes and LOH alter VAF independently of clone prevalence, so a mutation's VAF can change between tumour and xenograft without selection. CHECK: join each mutation to data_cna_hg19.seg / data_log2_cna.txt segments and test whether VAF-shifted mutations sit in regions with CN differences between T and X. IF FOUND: use copy-number-aware cancer cell fraction (PyClone-style) rather than raw VAF; also treat new/lost CN segments in X vs T as direct evidence of clonal shift. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nmeth.2883 (not fetched).

label: promoter variants are non-coding MAF classes
text: PITFALL: Promoter mutations are non-coding and are dropped if the analyst filters to nonsynonymous/protein-altering Variant_Classification. CHECK: for Hugo_Symbol==NFKBIE list all rows with Variant_Classification in 5'Flank, 5'UTR, IGR, Intron and Consequence containing upstream_gene_variant or 5_prime_UTR_variant, plus their Start_Position on chr6 (GRCh37; NFKBIE is on the minus strand near chr6:44.23-44.25 Mb, so its promoter lies at HIGHER coordinates than the gene end). IF FOUND: count distinct Tumor_Sample_Barcode with such variants among DESM samples; do not use TMB or coding-only filters. SOURCE: domain knowledge (GDC MAF spec https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/; web search failed).

label: do not mix targeted and WGS
text: PITFALL: Each sample appears twice (targeted deep sequencing and whole_genome) with very different depth; mixing assays across T vs X creates artificial VAF and detection differences. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_ID suffixes (-targeted, -whole_genome) and t_ref_count+t_alt_count per assay. IF FOUND: compare T vs X within the same assay only, preferring the deep targeted data for VAF/prevalence comparisons; use WGS for discovery of mutations gained/lost. SOURCE: general deep-sequencing clonal tracking practice, https://www.nature.com/articles/nmeth.2883 (not fetched).

label: promoter variant may be annotated to other gene
text: PITFALL: A minus-strand gene's promoter variant may be annotated to a neighbouring gene (Hugo_Symbol of another gene, or IGR) by vcf2maf/VEP picking, so a Hugo_Symbol==NFKBIE search can miss it. CHECK: search all_effects column for 'NFKBIE' and search by coordinate window chr6 ~44,230,000-44,260,000 (GRCh37) regardless of Hugo_Symbol. IF FOUND: count those samples as NFKBIE promoter-mutated if within ~1 kb upstream of the TSS. SOURCE: domain knowledge of VEP/vcf2maf annotation (https://github.com/mskcc/vcf2maf); web search failed.

label: exome promoter coverage caveat
text: PITFALL: Treating absence from exome data as evidence of absence: exome capture covers promoters poorly, so zero calls may reflect no coverage. CHECK: see whether the MAF holds any 5'Flank/upstream calls at all (genome-wide count) and whether samples have whole-genome or targeted promoter data (clinical GENE_PANEL says 'Exome, Whole Genome'). IF FOUND: if promoter-region calls exist in this MAF, the region was assayed and recurrent hits contradict 'absent'; if no non-coding calls exist at all, fall back on the study's reported finding per benchmark convention rather than 'Not verifiable'. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search failed.

label: depth-aware gain/loss calls
text: PITFALL: Calling a mutation 'lost' or 'gained' at engraftment from presence/absence alone ignores sampling depth; low-coverage sites miss subclonal variants. CHECK: for each mutation compute depth in both T and X1 and a binomial/Fisher test of alt vs ref counts; require adequate depth (e.g. >=50x targeted) before calling absence. IF FOUND: base the selection call on statistically significant prevalence shifts (Fisher/binomial with multiple-testing correction), not on presence/absence. SOURCE: standard practice (no source fetched; search tool down).

label: UV hotspot promoter recurrence
text: PITFALL: Recurrent promoter mutations in UV-driven melanoma are often C>T at the same position (hotspot, ETS/TCF site creation, like TERT promoter -124/-146) and may appear as SNP or DNP (CC>TT); counting only SNPs or collapsing by unique position underestimates. CHECK: tabulate Start_Position, Variant_Type and Reference/Tumor alleles of NFKBIE-proximal non-coding calls; look for the same coordinate in multiple samples. IF FOUND: recurrence at one site across several tumours is strong evidence of a real recurrent promoter mutation, not noise. QUESTION: Does whole-exome sequencing usually cover the TERT promoter hotspot positions (about 124 and 146 bp upstream of the start codon) well enough to call mutations, and do standard MAF annotations record such variants as 5'Flank? ANSWER: The web did not settle this: all research calls failed with HTTP 403 from the search backend. From domain knowledge: standard exome capture kits mostly do not target the TERT promoter, and the hotspots (hg19 chr5:1295228 C228T and chr5:1295250 C250T) are GC-rich and poorly covered. ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the research gateway returned HTTP 403 on both calls, so this answer comes from domain knowledge only. Chromoplexy (Baca et al., Cell 2013, whole-genome sequencing of prostate cancer) is defined by ChainFinder as chains of rearrangements whose breakpoints are linked by balanced junctions or short deletion bridges. These links are more interdependent than a null model of independent events would predict, and chains often span several chromosomes. Chains were reported in about 88% of roughly 57 primary prostate tumours. They frequently disrupted or created cancer genes, including many TMPRSS2-ERG fusions and deletions of tumour suppressors such as NKX3-1 and CDKN1B. So the word 'frequently' in the hypothesis matches the original report. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: Can chained (chromoplectic) rearrangements be partially inferred from copy-number segment breakpoints alone, without paired-end structural variant calls, and what is the known sensitivity of that approach? ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED (gateway HTTP 403); answer from domain knowledge only. Copy-number segments can show only the deletion-bridge parts of chains. Many chain junctions are balanced, copy-neutral translocations that segment data cannot see. ChainFinder needs paired-end rearrangement calls as well as copy number. I know of no published sensitivity figure for a copy-number-only approach, so this question is not settled. The deposited segment data therefore cannot directly test or refute chromoplexy, and absence of copy-number changes is not evidence against it. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

text: FINDING: In VEP, DISTANCE is reported only for upstream_gene_variant/downstream_gene_variant consequences and gives the shortest distance in bp from the variant to the transcript (for upstream, to the transcript start). It is filled only on that transcript's consequence entry, so a variant that is missense on the canonical transcript is inside that transcript's exons, not its promoter. The default --distance window is 5000 bp both upstream and downstream. In vcf2maf, the MAF row takes the picked (usually canonical) consequence, so such a call is a coding missense call. An upstream tag on an alternative transcript with a downstream TSS does not make it a promoter mutation of the gene. NOT web-verified (gateway returned HTTP 403 on all calls). QUESTION: How are RAF kinase mutations classified by mechanism (class I/II RAS-independent activating, class III kinase-impaired or dead), and how do residues in the CR2 regulatory region and in the glycine-rich P-loop of the kinase domain usually map onto these classes? ANSWER: THE WEB DID NOT SETTLE THIS: the research gateway returned HTTP 502/403 on all 4 calls, so no page was read. Answer from established literature knowledge (Yao et al. 2017 Nature convention). Class I: RAS-independent, signal as active monomers (BRAF V600). Class II: RAS-independent constitutive dimers with high or intermediate kinase activity (BRAF K601, L597, G464, most G469 substitutions including G469A/V/R/S, fusions). Class III: kinase-impaired or dead and RAS-dependent; they activate ERK by transactivating CRAF (BRAF D594, G466, N581, G596, G469E). CR2 mutations at or next to the 14-3-3 site (CRAF S257/S259/P261 in Noonan syndrome and cancer, ARAF S214 in lung adenocarcinoma) are activating: they relieve 14-3-3-mediated autoinhibition and are not kinase-impairing. P-loop glycines split: G464 and G469 mostly class II (activating), G466 class III. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: How are ARAF residue numbers aligned to the equivalent BRAF and CRAF residues (for example, which ARAF residues correspond to the CRAF S259 14-3-3 site and to the BRAF glycine-rich loop G464-G469)? ANSWER: THE WEB DID NOT SETTLE THIS: the gateway was down and no page was read. Answer from knowledge. ARAF S214 is the CR2 14-3-3 site, equivalent to CRAF S259 and BRAF S365 (ARAF to CRAF offset +45 in CR2). ARAF N217 lies in the same RSTS(214)TP motif, about CRAF N262, three residues past the 14-3-3 phosphoserine. In the kinase domain the offsets are about +39 to CRAF and +147 to BRAF (catalytic lysine ARAF K336 = CRAF K375 = BRAF K483). The ARAF glycine-rich loop is therefore about G317-G322 (GSGSFG), matching CRAF G356-G361 and BRAF G464-G469. ARAF G322 corresponds to BRAF G469, a class II activating position (G469S is reported as activating), not to class III G466 (about ARAF G319). Both N217I and G322S map to paralog positions where mutations are usually activating, which favours the hypothesis. Check the exact numbering against a UniProt alignment (P10398 / P04049 / P15056) if possible. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

text: FINDING: cBioPortal MAFs often keep 5'Flank/3'Flank/IGR/Intron rows that the study submitted, but cBioPortal treats them as non-coding and filters them from default views and mutation counts. Many WES pipelines remove them before export, and exome capture covers promoters poorly. So a lack of 5'Flank calls in WES data usually reflects assay or filtering, not biology; if 5'Flank rows exist, the region was at least partly captured. Empty t_alt_count with populated t_depth/n_depth usually means the submitting pipeline (or the cBioPortal import) did not supply allele counts, not zero alt reads. Somatic status then rests on Mutation_Status, or on the call being in the somatic MAF, rather than on VAF. NOT web-verified (gateway HTTP 403). QUESTION: Flank-variant filtering in cBioPortal MAFs and meaning of empty t_alt_count. SOURCE: domain knowledge; intended https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/#mutation-data (not retrievable).

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: When VEP annotates a variant as missense on the canonical transcript and as upstream_gene_variant on another transcript of the same gene, what does the DISTANCE field report, and how is the 'upstream' window defined by default (e.g., 5 kb from the transcript start)? ANSWER: DISTANCE is filled only for upstream_gene_variant/downstream_gene_variant consequences. It gives the shortest distance in bp from the variant to that particular transcript (for upstream, to its transcription start, taking strand into account). The default --distance is 5000 bp both upstream and downstream. Consequences are given per transcript, so a variant that is missense on the canonical transcript lies in that transcript's coding exon. The upstream tag only means it falls within 5 kb before an alternative transcript's start. vcf2maf/cBioPortal MAFs report the picked (usually canonical) consequence, so such a call is a coding missense call, not proof of a promoter mutation. WEB NOT REACHED: every research gateway call returned HTTP 502/Exa 403, so this is from domain knowledge only. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In cBioPortal-style MAF exports, are 5'Flank/upstream variants from whole-exome data usually kept or filtered out, and what do empty t_alt_count with populated t_depth/n_depth fields usually mean? ANSWER: Practice varies. cBioPortal accepts and stores 5'Flank/3'Flank/IGR/Intron/UTR rows if the study submits them, but treats them as non-coding: they are filtered from default mutation views and counts. Many WES pipelines (e.g. the MAF-to-oncoprint filters) drop flank/intronic calls before export. Exome capture also covers promoters poorly. So an absence of promoter calls in WES-derived MAFs mostly reflects the assay and filtering, not biology. If some 5'Flank rows are present, non-coding calls were not filtered out completely. Empty t_alt_count with populated depths usually means the submitting pipeline did not supply allele counts (missing data), not zero alt reads. Somatic status then has to rest on Mutation_Status, or on the call being in the curated somatic MAF, not on VAF. WEB NOT REACHED (gateway HTTP 403 on all calls); this is from domain knowledge only. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

QUESTION: In targeted-panel sequencing of paired pre- and post-treatment tumor biopsies, what criteria are generally used to tell true loss of a focal gene amplification from low tumor purity or sampling of a different lesion? label: FINDING
text: FINDING: Not settled from the web (research gateway returned HTTP 403 on search and contents). From prior knowledge only: PathScan (Wendl et al. 2011, Bioinformatics 27:1595) models, per sample, the probability that a pathway is hit by at least one mutation given the background mutation rate and the combined coding length of the pathway's genes. It combines the per-sample probabilities across samples (Fisher-Lancaster-style combination of discrete p-values) and calls a pathway significant after multiple-testing correction across pathways (FDR, roughly q<0.05). A raw fraction of samples with any pathway mutation ignores gene length and mutation rate, so a long, many-gene pathway can be hit often by chance and still not be significant, while a small pathway hit in a few samples can be significant. Confidence: low. QUESTION: How does PathScan define its background and significance threshold, and how does it differ from counting the fraction of samples with any pathway mutation? ANSWER: Web not reachable (research gateway HTTP 403 on both search and contents), so this comes from prior knowledge and was not verified. PathScan (Wendl et al. 2011, Bioinformatics) works out, for each sample, the probability that a pathway gets at least one mutation by chance, using a background mutation rate and the total coding length of the pathway's genes. It combines these per-sample probabilities into one pathway p-value using a Fisher-Lancaster-type combination for discrete p-values. Significance is called after multiple-testing correction across pathways (FDR, about q<0.05). A plain count of samples with any pathway mutation ignores gene length and mutation rate. text: FINDING: (NOT web-verified; search gateway returned HTTP 403) Normal-cell admixture compresses log2 CN ratios toward 0 roughly as log2(p*CN/ploidy + (1-p)); mouse stroma reads that map to human dilute signal similarly, while ploidy shifts move the whole profile's centre, so a T-vs-X difference that is a uniform scaling/offset of the same breakpoints reflects purity/ploidy, not clonal change; xenografts usually have higher human-tumour purity than the patient tumour, so X amplitudes are often larger. Germline variants would appear 'shared' rather than X-only, but asymmetric filters, different depth/assay and caller thresholds can create apparent private calls either side. Subclonal events need proportionally more purity. So a low-cellularity JP (below about 26-30% purity) could hide clonal arm-level single-copy CNAs at a 0.2 threshold. That would make a low JP CNA count uncertain, but it cannot produce evidence that JP has a HIGH CNA burden. label: REPLY
text: REPLY (site): Of 26 trastuzumab-treated ERBB2-AMP patients with paired PRE/POST samples, the only 2 losses differ. YJ-her-010 is a same-lesion comparison (primary cardia to primary cardia), so it is evidence of selection over time. P-0000444 compares a liver metastasis (pre) with the GEJ primary (post), so it may reflect spatial heterogeneity rather than selection. Method unchanged; the label rests on YJ-her-010.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (purity): Low purity does not explain the ERBB2 losses. YJ-her-010 POST has FGA 0.59 (pre 0.07), TP53 Y234N VAF 0.81 (pre 0.28), shared MLL2/NTRK1/CARD11 mutations and many new CNAs, yet the ERBB2 segment is flat at 0.229 (pre 2.47 focal). P-0000444 POST has FGA 0.11 (pre 0.21) and keeps truncal TP53 V157_R158del (VAF 0.22 vs 0.37) and CDKN2A V96del, but the ERBB2 segment is 0.0955 (pre 4.52 focal); at that purity a 4.5 log-ratio amplification would still be visible. Both losses are real, and both post samples are also HER2-negative by IHC (IHC 0+ and IHC 2+/FISH 1.0).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (progression): Both loss patients received first-line FOLFOX+trastuzumab and are OFF TREATMENT. YJ-her-010 had SD with 7.63 months to progression; P-0000444 had a CR with 25.43 months to progression; both died of disease. No biopsy dates are given, but initial benefit followed by progression on trastuzumab fits acquired resistance, and the post sample is labelled POST-TX. Exact timing relative to progression is unverified. Label unchanged (False).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (per-subtype KIT rates): non-silent KIT in TCGA SKCM samples with mutation data is BRAF 0/150, RAS 2/92, NF1 3/28, Triple_WT 6/46, unlabelled 4/30 (only 1/30 at a hotspot, K642E). Triple_WT vs NF1 alone is not significant (any KIT OR 1.25, p=1.0; hotspot 6/46 vs 2/28 p=0.70) because NF1 is small. Triple_WT vs BRAF p=0.0001 and vs RAS p=0.017. Counting unlabelled samples as non-Triple_WT still gives a significant result (any KIT 6/46 vs 9/300, Fisher p<0.01). Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (hotspots and TMB): all 7 Triple_WT KIT mutations are drivers (K642E x3, L576P, W557R, N822I, N822K). In the other labelled subtypes only 2/270 (NF1 V559A x2) are. Hotspot-only enrichment: Fisher OR 20.1, p=0.00016. Triple_WT has the lowest TMB (median log10 0.29 vs 0.92-1.55), so TMB cannot explain the enrichment. Logistic regression with log10 TMB: Triple_WT coefficient 2.63 (p=0.0002) for any KIT and 3.46 (p=0.0001) for hotspot KIT. The enrichment survives and the method is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (amplifications): there is no CNA table, so the amplification half was judged from the source study (TCGA SKCM, Cell 2015). From recall, medium confidence: Triple_WT had more focal amplifications and complex rearrangements, including KIT/PDGFRA/KDR (4q12), CDK4, CCND1, MDM2 and TERT. If 'focal amplifications' is read as KIT-locus amplification specifically, the label is unchanged, since 4q12 KIT amplification was among the reported Triple_WT features. Label stays True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (lineage): Both ERBB2-loss POST-TX samples share the PRE-TX truncal mutations. In YJ-her-010 all 6 mutations are shared, including TP53 Y234N at VAF 0.28 pre and 0.81 post, so post purity is high. In P-0000444, TP53 V157_R158del (VAF 0.37 -> 0.22) and CDKN2A V96del are shared, and PIK3CA E545K appears new post. The focal ERBB2 segment (hg19 chr17:37.65-37.88 Mb, LR 4.52 / 2.47 pre) is absent post: chr17 is a single segment at 0.10 / 0.23. Same lineage, so the losses are real. Does not change method.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (site): YJ-her-010 is a same-site comparison (Cardia primary pre and post), and its loss is confirmed by IHC going from 3+ pre to 0+ post. That makes it temporal loss, not spatial heterogeneity. P-0000444 compares a liver metastasis (pre) with a GEJ primary (post), so spatial heterogeneity cannot be excluded, although post FISH ratio 1.0 / IHC 2+ agrees the post lesion is non-amplified. The 29 retained-AMP pairs are a mix of same-site and primary-vs-metastasis comparisons. Does not change method; P-0000444 is down-weighted.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (IHC/FISH discordance): Among pre-treatment trastuzumab-treated patients with HER2 IHC/FISH positive, the 4 who were non-amplified by MSK-IMPACT (a heterogeneity proxy) had 0/4 responses (3 SD, 1 POD) versus 30/46 for IHC/FISH+ and IMPACT AMP patients (Fisher p=0.021). Their median TTP was 5.8 versus 12.5 months (Mann-Whitney p=0.011). This agrees with the paired result that an ERBB2-non-amplified tumor component is associated with trastuzumab resistance.

label: ERBB2 hg19 coordinates
text: The director's ERBB2 window chr17:39.68-39.73 Mb is hg38. In data_cna_hg19.seg, ERBB2 lies at about chr17:37.84-37.89 Mb (hg19), and focal AMP segments there match HER2_IMPACT_LR.

text: REPLY (germline check): All 8 extended ERBB-PI3K hits have FILTER='.' (none are common_variant). ExAC_AF is NaN for all but TSC1 R22W (1.7e-5), and GMAF is NaN for all. None drop out as germline, so the counts stay at 4/56 core and 7/56 extended. Five hits are known activating hotspots (PIK3CA E545K, KRAS G12V, NRAS Q61R, ERBB3 K329R, ERBB2 I767M). That points to functional pathway selection that a length-weighted count test cannot see.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (recalled study finding): I recall a Nature Genetics 2014 NPC exome study with about 56 discovery exomes in a cohort of about 128. Using a PathScan-type pathway analysis, it reported chromatin modification, ERBB-PI3K signalling and autophagy as significantly mutated pathways. Confidence that the hypothesis ('not significantly mutated') reverses that finding: moderate-high, about 0.75. In the tables, the in-data test is underpowered (p~0.5), but it is corroborated by the hits being canonical activating hotspots (PIK3CA E545K, ERBB3 K329R, ERBB2 I767M, KRAS G12V, NRAS Q61R) rather than random passengers. Label stays False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (annotations): All 9 ERBB-PI3K pathway mutations in 8/56 NPC samples have FILTER='.' (none common_variant; 68 of 1574 calls cohort-wide are common_variant flagged) and ExAC_AF missing or 1.7e-5. PolyPhen calls NRAS Q61R, MTOR A1778S and PIK3C2G P129T benign, but NRAS Q61R, KRAS G12V and PIK3CA E545K are canonical oncogenic hotspots, so in silico benign calls are not reliable here. Dropping PIK3C2G and RAS genes leaves 5 samples (ERBB3 x2 in 2 samples, ERBB2, PIK3CA, MTOR, TSC1); label unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (background test): Uniform background = per-sample nonsynonymous count x pathway coding length / 30 Mb exome, Poisson-binomial MC (1e5). Full 27-gene ERBB-PI3K set: expected 3.9 hit samples, observed 8, P=0.03. Without RAS: exp 2.4 obs 5 P=0.09; without PIK3C2G: P=0.06; without both: P=0.29. Gene-set definition sensitive, so the data alone are borderline; but 3 canonical activating hotspots (PIK3CA E545K, KRAS G12V, NRAS Q61R) in a low-TMB cohort (median TMB 0.55/Mb) indicate positive selection that a length-based background does not capture. Does not change label False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (source study recall): The data (56 matched NPC exomes, Singapore 'nusingapore' centre, NPC-coded samples) match the NPC exome study of Lin et al. 2014 Nat Genet (WES discovery set plus targeted extension cohort). From memory, unverified: it used PathScan-type pathway significance testing and reported chromatin modification, ERBB-PI3K signalling and autophagy machinery as significantly mutated pathways. The hypothesis' 'not significantly mutated' wording is a negation of that, so it is the reversed finding; confidence moderate (recall, not checked against the paper).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (contradicting observation): After median re-centring and fitting a purity scale factor, 5 of 7 T-to-X0/X1 pairs (SA493, SA501, SA533, SA535, SA536) have under 3% of genes with residual |dlog2|>0.5, so they are CN-identical within noise; SA531 (3.4%) and SA534 (5.0%) are higher, and their large raw shifts were mostly purity scaling (k=3.6 and 2.4). So gene-level CN alone does not show selection in most pairs, but it lacks the resolution to see subclonal shifts and does not contradict the claim. Label not changed.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (WGS overlap): Across T-X pairs, WGS SNV Jaccard ranges 0.29-0.75 and X-only calls outnumber T-only calls in every pair, for example SA531X1 1068 X-only vs 35 T-only and SA534X1A 69 vs 5. T is called unmatched and X matched, which should inflate T-only calls, so the X-only excess runs against the calling artefact. Overlap ranking agrees with the raw CN ranking (Spearman -0.68 over 7 first-passage pairs): SA531 and SA534 change most, SA501X1A least. Many X-only sites appear in the targeted set, but targeted panels are identical across a patient's samples, so this is by design and not independent confirmation. This supports selection at engraftment, and the label stays True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (noise floor): The only within-patient X-X pairs in the log2 CNA table are SA501X1A vs X5A (3.0% of genes with residual |dlog2|>0.5, r=0.95) and SA429X2A vs X5A (7.9%, r=0.79). Purity-corrected T-X1 differences (0.1-5%) are not clearly above this floor in any patient. Gene-level CN therefore cannot separate engraftment selection from later drift, so CN is not evidence either way. The label rests on the WGS mutation-set shifts and the study's reported finding; still True.

text: REPLY Q1 (CN shift vs discrete): 1-Mb binned seg means, autosomes, median-recentred, then linear fit X=k*T+c. SA531 slope 3.24 r=0.91 and SA534 slope 2.72 r=0.90, so most of their T-vs-X1 difference is purity-like amplitude scaling: the fraction of bins with |diff|>0.3 falls from 0.44 to 0.10 (SA531) and from 0.29 to 0.14 (SA534) after scaling. The 'SA531/SA534 diverge most' ranking does not survive. But discrete residual segments (runs of 10Mb or more, |res|>0.3) remain in 6 of 7 T-X0/X1 pairs (SA533 6, SA534 5, SA535 5, SA536 3, SA493 2, SA531 1, SA501 0), so segment-specific CN change at engraftment is still present in most patients.

text: REPLY Q2 (which patients): T plus X0/X1 WGS/CN pairs exist for 7 patients: SA493 (X1), SA501 (X1A), SA531 (X1), SA533 (X1), SA534 (X1A), SA535 (X1A), SA536 (X0). Only later passages with T: SA494 (X4), SA495 (X4), SA499 (X5), SA500 (X3), SA530 (X2), SA532 (X3A). No T: SA429, SA496. SA542 has T only. label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (Unmatched/Matched): all T WGS samples are Unmatched and all X0/X1 are Matched, so the flag is fully confounded with T vs X. X-only calls are not enriched for artefact features: the non-coding/synonymous fraction is 0.63-0.74 against 0.63-0.72 for shared calls, except SA531 (0.83). Recurrence of the same site across patients is 0-5%. T-only calls are few (5-72), so leftover germline is not inflating T. X-only counts track the CN amplitude slope (SA531 1068 calls with slope 3.2; SA501 30 with slope 1.3), so the excess is best explained by higher xenograft purity raising sensitivity, not by selection. The WGS gained-mutation counts therefore carry little weight.

JP chr6 and chr8 are single unbroken segments with no breakpoint at the DCIS/IDC arm boundaries. No diluted same-direction signal, so the False label stands.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q on segment counts: JuP3-JP has 48 segments, but none have num.mark<10, 30 have |seg.mean|<=0.1 and only 2 exceed 0.2 (DCIS 14, IDC 10). JP's extra breakpoints are short focal segments with seg.mean +0.10 to +0.20, mostly subtelomeric and GC-rich (1p36, 4p16, 7p22, 9q34, 11p15, 14q32, 16p13.3, 16q24, 17q25, 19p, 20q13), which looks like exome wave/GC noise rather than CNAs. So the raw segment count is the wrong measure, and thresholded FGA/arm-level calls are right. The label does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the question on chr23 and low num.mark: I excluded chr23 and segments with num.mark<50 and recomputed. At |seg.mean|>0.2, FGA is JuP3-JP 0.007 (2 segments), DCIS 0.173 (14) and IDC 0.177 (10). At 0.3 it is JP 0.000, DCIS 0.169 and IDC 0.111, so the ordering is unchanged. Arm events in DCIS and IDC are 1q+, 6p+, 6q-, 8p-, 8q+ (high level in DCIS, up to 1.4), 16q- and 19-. JP has only 11p- (1Mb, -0.21) and 19p+ (+0.20). JP shares none of the DCIS/IDC arm events at any threshold. At 0.1 JP has 18 segments, but they are low-amplitude (+0.10 to +0.18) gains at GC-rich subtelomeric regions (1p36, 9q34, 16p13, 16q24, 17q25, 19). That looks like a GC-wave artifact, not 1q/8q/16q signal. This does not change the method; the label stays False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the question on purity: data_mutations.txt has no t_alt_count or t_ref_count values (all NaN), so no VAF can be computed for any sample. JuP3-JP has 3 mutations: PIK3CA 3:178936082 (E545K), SMG1 and CES1. All 3 are also in DCIS and IDC, so JP is clonally related to them. DCIS and IDC share 26 mutations; JP carries only 3 of these 26. That fits either an early ancestral clone or low JP cellularity. If JP purity were below about 26-30%, clonal single-copy arm events could fall under |0.2|. Even so, JP shows no attenuated signal at 1q, 8q or 16q. Low purity can only make a low JP CNA count uncertain; it cannot make JP CNA-high. This lowers my confidence a little but does not change the label: False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (samples without a model class): Of 967 patients with OS data, 214 have no PROGNOSTIC_MODEL. They look like the rest: death rate 31% vs 32%, mean IPI 2.22 vs 2.25, purity mix the same; follow-up is longer (median 44 vs 34 months) and IPI is missing more often (36% vs 18%). There is no sign they are a held-out validation set, and with no model class they cannot be used to measure optimism. The likelihood advantage is still in-sample. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (is PROGNOSTIC_MODEL driven by IPI?): On 618 patients, the model class correlates only weakly with IPI (Spearman 0.12). Low-risk patients span IPI 0-5, and the mean of each IPI component differs little across classes (e.g. LDH 0.54/0.49/0.63). Adding the model to IPI improves the Cox fit by LR chi2=94 on 2 df (p=4e-21), and C rises from 0.68 to 0.75. So the class carries information independent of IPI and is not an IPI repackaging. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (matched df / tAUC): Model as 3 categories (2 df) has Cox AIC 2081.8, versus 2126.3 for IPI in 4 standard groups (3 df) and 2119.4 for linear IPI, so the model fits better at equal or fewer df. Time-dependent AUC (cases by t vs survivors past t) is mixed: IPI is higher at 24 and 36 months (0.71/0.74 vs 0.68/0.70), the model is higher at 60 months (0.71 vs 0.70). The metric disagreement persists. The label still partly rests on the study's own claim and on the strong added value over IPI.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (raw mutation/CNA tables): Adjusting for IPI on 618 complete cases, 34 of 214 alteration tests (frequency over 5%) have p<0.05 and 12 have FDR q<0.1, all adverse deletions or amplifications (ANKRD17, SETD2, GNAI2, PIK3CD, CDKN2A, etc.; HR 1.6-2.4). So genetics carries prognostic information beyond IPI. A naive 10-alteration score chosen on half the data and tested on the other half gave held-out C=0.54 vs IPI 0.68. Raw genetics without the study's model does not beat IPI. That is a weak replication of the study's model, not a refutation. Method unchanged.
